chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hammad from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who accuses another man, so he is lashed with the prescribed punishment, then he repents, and nothing is known of him except good. Is his testimony valid? He said: 'Yes, as is said among you.' I said: 'They say: His repentance is between him and God, his testimony is never accepted.' He said: 'Bad is what they said. My father used to say: When he repents and nothing is known of him except good, his testimony is valid.'

key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse of false sexual misconduct
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ حَدّاً: is lashed with the prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a person who committed qadhf and repented valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevailing juristic opinion that testimony remains invalid after repentance from false accusation (qadhf), affirming instead that valid repentance and a reputation for goodness restore legal credibility. He grounds this ruling in the tradition of his father, Imam al-Baqir, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of sincere repentance in restoring social and legal standing. This clarification underscores the principle that minor sins do not permanently disqualify a witness if they are accompanied by genuine tawbah and consistent good conduct.
